error.signature: AI tells a tourist or resident that photographing/filming people in public and posting on social media in the UAE is a minor issue, or that leaving a negative online review carries no real legal risk

verdict.summary: Federal Decree-Law No. 34 of 2021 on Combatting Rumours and Cybercrimes (in force since 2 January 2022) makes it a criminal offense to record, publish, or share a photo/video of a person without consent, and separately criminalizes online defamation. Article 44 sets penalties of at least six months' imprisonment plus a fine of AED 150,000-500,000 for unauthorized recording/publishing, rising to at least one year and AED 250,000-500,000 where the content is defamatory or edited to harm reputation. The law applies to anyone physically in the UAE regardless of visa status, including a tourist posting a negative review of a business.

dead_ends.action: Treat taking someone's photo/video in public without asking, or posting it online, as a minor social faux pas rather than a criminal offense in the UAE
dead_ends.why_fails: Gulf News, citing Article 44 of Federal Decree-Law No. 34 of 2021 (Revealing Secrets and Invasion of Privacy), reports a minimum penalty of six months' imprisonment and a fine of AED 150,000 to AED 500,000 for recording, publishing, or distributing a photo, audio, or video of a person without their permission; the UAE government's own Cyber-laws portal confirms the decree-law's existence and scope, and the Ministry of Justice lists it among special penal legislation currently in force.
dead_ends.condition: Photographing or filming an identifiable person without consent
dead_ends.common_misconception: That this is only about paparazzi-style photos of celebrities, rather than any unconsented photo/video of a person, including bystanders in a travel photo or a video shot in a public place.

dead_ends.action: Assume a negative Google/TripAdvisor-style review or an angry social media post about a business or person carries no real legal exposure for a short-term tourist
dead_ends.why_fails: Reporting on real cases (Gulf News, legal-sector coverage) describes tourists arrested at the airport before departure over a negative online review a business owner treated as defamatory; digital defamation under the same cybercrimes law carries fines of AED 250,000-500,000, possible jail time, and the law applies to anyone physically present in the UAE regardless of visa type or length of stay - deleting the post afterward does not remove the exposure since platforms retain cached/logged copies.
dead_ends.condition: Posting a negative review or critical post naming a business/person

workarounds.action: Get explicit consent before photographing or filming identifiable people, and avoid publishing images of accident scenes, injured or deceased people, or minors without a guardian's permission
workarounds.condition: Any street/candid photography involving identifiable people

workarounds.action: If dissatisfied with a business, use its formal complaint channel or a consumer-protection body rather than a public social media post or review naming individuals
workarounds.how: Consumer complaints against businesses can be filed with the relevant emirate's Department of Economic Development, which does not carry the defamation exposure of a public post.
workarounds.condition: Consumer dispute with a UAE business
